title: The Eye of the Pantheon
synopsis: The Owl's next clue is under the round eye of the Pantheon.
A parcel waits for the detective who knows the password.
Inside is the missing piece... or is it?
goal: Find the Owl's parcel and test what is inside.

options.label: The stone with a ship
options.feedback: The light is on the ship at 10:00. Where is it two hours later?

options.label: The stone with a lion
options.feedback: The lion is only one hour after the ship. The card says two hours.

options.label: The stone with a key
options.feedback: The key is three hours after the ship. Count again from 10:00.

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene) inside the Pantheon: the Owl's card and the guide sign lie on the bench by the door; the floor stones open once it is read. The four stones are told apart by their carvings (ship, lion, book, key).

Coordinates measured on the made pantheon_hall.png (1536x1024, sha256 d960679b186dda4b…) with a 100px grid overlay, STEP 3-15B B1. The bench area stops at y 880 and the stones start below it at x 1095+, so the two never overlap.

STEP 3-15B B3: the opening narrowed to x 300-1350 (the plain columns on the left and the bronze door on the right left outside, reached by a drag), so a phone opens the hall about 1.46 times larger; the full height is kept so the eye, the light, the card and the stones are all on screen as it opens. Coordinates and measuredOn unchanged.

clueInputs.note: The Owl's card in Box 7: go where the roof has a round eye.

learning.objective: 부엉이 카드의 'two hours after the ship'과 안내판의 시각을 읽고, 바닥 돌 그림 중 책이 새겨진 돌을 고른다.
expressions: The sun moves the light like a clock hand.

play.title: The Round Eye
story: The Pantheon has a big round hole in its roof. People call it the eye.
A circle of sunlight moves slowly across the floor.
Somewhere in here, the Owl left a card.
play.letterIntro: On the bench, an owl card and a guide sign:
play.letter:
THE OWL CARD:
Look for the stone the light falls on two hours after the ship.
That stone tells you where my parcel waits.
— The Owl

GUIDE SIGN — THE LIGHT FROM THE EYE:
The sun moves the light like a clock hand.
10:00 — on the stone with a SHIP
11:00 — on the stone with a LION
12:00 — on the stone with a BOOK
1:00 — on the stone with a KEY
play.question: Which stone does the Owl mean?
hints: Find the card on the bench by the door and read it first.
The light is on the ship at 10:00. Count two hours on the guide sign.
transition: Two hours after the ship, the light falls on the book stone.
Across the square, there is a small old bookshop.

clue.title: The Book Stone
clue.note: Two hours after the ship, the light is on the book. The parcel is at a bookshop.

evidence.name: The Pantheon Owl Card

explore.task: Look around the Pantheon. Find the Owl's card.

discovery.title: TWO HOURS AFTER THE SHIP
discovery.detail: The book stone tells you where the Owl's parcel waits.

notes: Letter: the Owl's note to the bookseller. The password is the opposite of lost.

clueInputs.note: The book stone sends you to the bookshop.
The Owl's first card: the piece is not lost.

learning.objective: the opposite of lost를 이해해 반대말 found를 쓴다.
expressions: The password is the opposite of lost.
Give it only to the detective who says the password.

play.title: The Password
story: The bookshop is small and full of old books.
An old bookseller looks at you over his glasses.
"A parcel? I can give it only to the right person. Read this."
play.letterIntro: The note to the bookseller says:
play.letter:
Dear bookseller,
Please keep my parcel safe.
Give it only to the detective who says the password.
The password is the opposite of LOST.
— The Owl
play.question: What is the password?
hints: Opposite means the other end, like big and small or hot and cold.
You lose a thing. Later you see it again. Now it is not lost. It is…
transition: The opposite of lost is found.
The bookseller brings out a heavy paper parcel.
On top is a card: "Test it before you trust it. — The Owl"

feedback.LOST: Lost is the word on the note. What is its opposite?
feedback.MISSING: Missing means almost the same as lost. What is the opposite?

play.orderFeedback: Check your spelling. It is the opposite of lost.

clue.title: The Password
clue.note: The bookseller kept the Owl's parcel for the detective who said the password.

evidence.name: The Owl's Note to the Bookseller
evidence.description: The Owl's note asking the bookseller to keep the parcel.
evidence.inscription: The password is the opposite of LOST.

discovery.title: THE OPPOSITE OF LOST
discovery.detail: The Owl keeps saying the piece is not lost. Now the parcel is yours.

notes: Letter: the Owl's test card, its steps out of order (First, Next, Last). Washing is not on the card.

learning.objective: First, Next, Last를 읽고 돌을 시험하는 순서를 놓는다. 카드에 없는 단계(wash)는 고르지 않는다.
expressions: First, weigh it on a scale.

play.title: Test It First
story: You open the parcel. Inside is a grey piece of stone with lines of old streets.
But the Owl's card says: test it before you trust it.
play.letter:
HOW TO TEST A STONE
Last, scratch a hidden corner with a coin.
First, weigh it on a scale.
Next, tap it and listen.
Do these three things, and you will know.
— The Owl
play.question: Put the Owl's three tests in order.
hints: Only three of the four steps are on the card.
Find First, then Next, then Last.
play.successMessage: You know how to test the stone!
transition: Weigh it, tap it, scratch it.
The bookseller has a scale for heavy books.
You start the tests. Giulia holds her breath.
play.orderFeedback: Read the card again: First, Next, Last. Is washing on it?

clue.title: Three Tests
clue.note: The Owl's three tests for a stone: weigh it, tap it, scratch a hidden corner.

evidence.name: The Owl's Test Card
evidence.description: The Owl's card with three tests for a stone.
evidence.inscription: First, weigh it. Next, tap it. Last, scratch a hidden corner.

discovery.title: TEST IT BEFORE YOU TRUST IT
discovery.detail: Is the stone in the parcel really the old map piece?

notes: Letter: the three test results and the Owl's note (marble is hard; plaster is soft and white). The piece in the parcel is plaster.

clueInputs.note: The three tests and what they show.
The dust was new, not old stone.
The same soft white dust as the bag in Box 7.

learning.objective: 세 가지 시험 결과(가볍다, thud, 부드러운 흰 가루)를 읽고 재료가 plaster임을 글자 타일로 맞춘다.
expressions: This piece is 4 kg. Too light!

play.title: What Is It Made Of?
story: The parcel has one more lock: a strip of letter tiles on the box.
play.letter:
WEIGH: The real piece is 12 kg. This piece is 4 kg. Too light!
TAP: Marble rings like a bell. This piece goes "thud".
SCRATCH: Soft white dust comes off, like chalk.

THE OWL'S NOTE:
Marble is hard stone. Plaster is soft and white.
Which one is this piece made of?
play.question: What is this piece really made of? Spell it.
hints: Is this piece hard or soft? Heavy or light?
The Owl's note names two things. Which one is soft and white?
play.successMessage: You found the truth about the piece!
transition: Someone made a copy of the map piece.
And someone put it in the glass case before Friday night.
The tiny paw print is your next clue.
play.orderFeedback: Every tile is right. Now read the Owl's note again.

evidence.name: The Plaster Copy
evidence.description: A copy of the map piece, light and soft. On its back: a paw print and a smudged number, No. 3?8.

play.evidenceLinkLine: The same soft white dust as the bag in Box 7.

ending.text: The same soft white dust as in Box 7.
So the Owl took a copy out of the case!
ending.speaker: giulia_marino

ending.text: On its back: a tiny paw print and No. 3?8.
Then where is the real piece?
ending.speaker: giulia_marino

hook: Someone made a plaster copy. Who made it, and where is the real piece?

learningGoal.title: Opposites and tests: found, first, next, last

objectives: Find the stone the light points to.
Test the piece in the parcel.
intro: The Pantheon is almost 2,000 years old.
Its round roof has a big hole at the top.
"The Owl's card said: the roof with a round eye," says Giulia. "Here we are!"
play.caseSummary: Under the Pantheon's round eye, the Owl's card led to a bookshop. With the password FOUND, you got the Owl's parcel. Three tests showed the piece inside is plaster. The Owl took a copy out of the glass case, not the real piece.

notes: Act 1's turn: the piece the Owl carried out was a plaster copy. The real piece was swapped before Friday.
The copy's paw print and No. 3?8 lead to the Bassi workshop in Case 05.
STEP 3-14: M1 is now a look round the Pantheon ending in a choice of four carved floor stones (new pictures). Discovery Moments and an ending added.
